records.issue_text: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally in update, so omitting the visible param silently sets it to false and wipes visibility on partial updates
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally (no `if params[:visible].present?`). If a client calls `PUT /admin/groups/:id` without a `visible` param, `params[:visible]` is `nil` and the expression evaluates to `false`, unintentionally clearing visibility on a partial update.

records.issue_text: `limit` in GroupsController#members is taken from params with no upper bound, allowing huge queries via limit=1000000
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is set directly from `params[:limit]` with only a default (`(params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and then passed to ActiveRecord `.limit(limit)` with no max clamp. This allows a client to request arbitrarily large pages (e.g., `limit=1000000`), creating a potential performance/DoS issue.

records.issue_text: `offset` in GroupsController#members is not validated/clamped, so a negative offset produces invalid SQL OFFSET and a 500 error
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and directly applies it via `.offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. A negative `offset` param will therefore become a negative integer and be passed to ActiveRecord, which can generate an invalid SQL `OFFSET` (e.g., `OFFSET -10`) and cause a 500. records.issue_text: `usernames.split(",")` in add_members assumes a String; an array param raises NoMethodError resulting in a 500 instead of 400/422
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the incoming `usernames` parameter is an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `split` is undefined and will raise `NoMethodError`, yielding a 500 instead of a handled 4xx. The diff shows no type check/coercion to String before `split`.

records.issue_text: add_members silently skips nonexistent usernames with no indication in the response, so admin typos get a success response
records.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is looked up with `User.find_by_username(username)`; if the user doesn’t exist it is simply skipped (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`). The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, with no indication that some/all usernames were invalid, so admin typos would still get a 200 success response.

records.issue_text: Group name is interpolated into the URL in group.js findMembers without encodeURIComponent, producing broken requests for names with spaces/special characters
admin-group.js addMembers never clears the usernames field after adding, so the stale value stays and re-submits the same members
records.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but never resets/clears `usernames` afterward (there’s even a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment). This means the input value can remain populated and clicking “Add” again would resend the same usernames.
